readings.title: Israel’s Oppression in Egypt
readings.subtitle: The New Pharaoh and the Oppression
readings.text: [Exodus 1:1] And these are the names of the sons of Yisra’el who came into Mitsrayim with <dn>את</dn> Ya’aqoḇ, each one with his household: [2] Re’uḇĕn, Shim’on, Lĕwi, and Yehuḏah; [3] Yissaḵar, Zeḇulun, and Benyamin; [4] Dan, and Naphtali, Gaḏ, and Ashĕr. [5] And all the beings who came from the loins of Ya’aqoḇ were seventy beings, and Yoseph was in Mitsrayim already. [6] And Yoseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation. [7] But the children of Yisra’el were fruitful and increased greatly, and multiplied and became extremely numerous, and the land was filled with <dn>את</dn> them. [8] Then a new sovereign arose over Mitsrayim, who did not know <dn>את</dn> Yoseph, [9] and he said to his people, “See, the people of the children of Yisra’el are more and mightier than we. [10] Come, let us act wisely towards them, lest they multiply, and it shall be when fightings occur, that they also join our enemies and fight against us, and go up out of the land.” [11] So they set slave-masters over them to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Par'oh storage cities, <dn>את</dn> Pithom and <dn>את</dn> Ra’amses. [12] But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were in dread of the children of Yisra’el. [13] And the Mitsrites made the children of Yisra’el serve with harshness, [14] and they made <dn>את</dn> their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar, and in brick, and in all kinds of service in the field – <dn>את</dn> all their service in which they made them serve was with harshness. [15] And the sovereign of Mitsrayim spoke to the Heḇrew midwives, of whom the name of one was Shiphrah and the name of the other Pu’ah, [16] and he said, “When you deliver the Heḇrew women, and see them on the birth-stool, if it is a son, then you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live.” [17] But the midwives feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and did not do as the sovereign of Mitsrayim commanded them, and kept the male children alive. [18] So the sovereign of Mitsrayim called for the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this, and kept the male children alive?” [19] And the midwives said to Par'oh, “Because the Heḇrew women are not like the Mitsrite women, for they are lively and give birth before the midwives come to them.” [20] And <dn>Elohim</dn> did good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became very numerous. [21] And it came to be, because the midwives feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, that <dn>He</dn> provided households for them. [22] And Par'oh commanded all his people, saying, “Every son who is born you are to throw into the river, but every daughter you are to keep alive.”

readings.title: The Birth of Moses
readings.subtitle: The Ark in the Reeds
readings.text: [Exodus 2:1] And a man of the house of Lĕwi went and married <dn>את</dn> a daughter of Lĕwi. [2] And the woman conceived and bore a son. And when she saw that he was a nice child, she hid him three months. [3] And when she could hide him no longer, she took an ark of wicker for him, and coated it with tar and pitch, and put <dn>את</dn> the child in it, and laid it in the reeds by the edge of the river. [4] And his sister stood at a distance, to know what would be done to him. [5] And the daughter of Par'oh came down to wash herself at the river, and her young women were walking by the river side. And when she saw <dn>את</dn> the ark among the reeds, she sent <dn>את</dn> her female slave to get it. [6] And she opened it and saw <dn>את</dn> the child, and see, the baby wept. So she had compassion on him, and said, “This is one of the Heḇrews’ children.” [7] And his sister said to Par'oh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call a nurse for you from the Heḇrew women, to nurse the child for you?” [8] And Par'oh’s daughter said to her, “Go.” And the young woman went and called the child’s mother. [9] And Par'oh’s daughter said to her, “Take <dn>את</dn> this child away and nurse him for me, and I shall give <dn>את</dn> your wages.” So the woman took <dn>את</dn> the child and nursed him. [10] And the child grew, and she brought him to Par'oh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Mosheh, saying, “Because I drew him out of the water.”

readings.title: Moses Flees to Midian
readings.subtitle: Escape to Midian
readings.text: [Exodus 2:11] And it came to be in those days, when Mosheh was grown, that he went out to his brothers and looked at their burdens. And he saw a Mitsrite striking a Heḇrew, one of his brothers. [12] So he turned this way and that way, and when he saw no one, he struck <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrite and hid him in the sand. [13] And he went out the second day and saw two Heḇrew men fighting, and he said to the one who did the wrong, “Why do you strike your neighbour?” [14] And he said, “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrite?” And Mosheh feared and said, “Truly, the matter is known!” [15] And Par'oh heard <dn>את</dn> of this matter, and he sought to kill <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. But Mosheh fled from the face of Par'oh and dwelt in the land of Miḏyan. And he sat down by a well. [16] And the priest of Miḏyan had seven daughters. And they came and drew water, and they filled <dn>את</dn> the troughs to water their father’s flock. [17] But the shepherds came and drove them away. Then Mosheh stood up and helped them, and watered <dn>את</dn> their flock. [18] And when they came to Re’u’ĕl their father, he said, “How is it that you have come so soon today?” [19] And they said, “A Mitsrite delivered us from the hand of the shepherds, and he also actually drew water for us and watered the flock.” [20] And he said to his daughters, “And where is he? Why did you leave <dn>את</dn> the man? Call him and let him eat bread.” [21] And Mosheh agreed to dwell with the man, and he gave <dn>את</dn> Tsiphorah his daughter to Mosheh. [22] And she bore a son, and he called <dn>את</dn> his name Gĕreshom, for he said, “I have been a sojourner in a foreign land.” [23] And it came to be in the course of those many days that the sovereign of Mitsrayim died. And the children of Yisra’el groaned because of the slavery, and they cried out. And their cry for help because of the slavery went up to <dn>Elohim</dn>. [24] And <dn>Elohim</dn> heard their groaning, and <dn>Elohim</dn> remembered <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> Aḇraham, with <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq, and with <dn>את</dn> Ya’aqoḇ. [25] And <dn>Elohim</dn> looked on <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’el, and <dn>Elohim</dn> knew.

readings.title: The Lineage of Moses and Aaron
readings.subtitle: The Lineage of the Leaders
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 6:1] The sons of Lĕwi: Gĕreshon, Qehath, and Merari. [2] And the sons of Qehath: Amram, Yitshar, and Ḥeḇron, and Uzzi’ĕl. [3] And the children of Amram: Aharon, and Mosheh, and Miryam.

readings.title: The Call of Moses
readings.subtitle: The Burning Bush
readings.text: [Exodus 3:1] And Mosheh was shepherding <dn>את</dn> the flock of Yithro his father-in-law, the priest of Miḏyan. And he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to Ḥorĕḇ, the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [2] And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush. And he looked and saw the bush burning with fire, but the bush was not consumed. [3] And Mosheh said, “I must turn aside now and see <dn>את</dn> this great sight, why the bush does not burn.” [4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw that he turned aside to see, and <dn>Elohim</dn> called to him from the midst of the bush and said, <dq>“Mosheh! Mosheh!”</dq> And he said, “Here I am.” [5] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Do not come near here. Take your sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is set-apart ground.”</dq> [6] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your father, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yitsḥaq, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya’aqoḇ.”</dq> And Mosheh hid his face, for he was afraid to look at <dn>Elohim</dn>. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have indeed seen <dn>את</dn> the oppression of <dn>My</dn> people who are in Mitsrayim, and have heard their cry because of their slave-masters, for <dn>I</dn> know <dn>את</dn> their sorrows.</dq> [8] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> have come down to deliver them from the hand of the Mitsrites, and to bring them up from that land to a good and spacious land, to a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Kena’anites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hiwwites and the Yeḇusites.</dq> [9] <dq>And now, see, the cry of the children of Yisra’el has come to <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> have also seen <dn>את</dn> the oppression with which the Mitsrites oppress them.</dq> [10] <dq>And now, come, <dn>I</dn> am sending you to Par'oh, and you bring <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people, the children of Yisra’el, out of Mitsrayim.”</dq> [11] And Mosheh said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Who am I that I should go to Par'oh, and that I should bring <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’el out of Mitsrayim?” [12] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Because <dn>I</dn> am with you. And this is the sign for you that <dn>I</dn> have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Mitsrayim, you are to serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> on this mountain.”</dq> [13] And Mosheh said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “See, when I come to the children of Yisra’el and say to them, ‘The <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they say to me, ‘What is <dn>His Name</dn>?’ what shall I say to them?” [14] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am that which <dn>I</dn> am.”</dq> And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra’el, ‘<dn>I Am</dn> has sent me to you.’ ”</dq> [15] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said further to Mosheh, <dq>“Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra’el, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of your fathers, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yitsḥaq, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya’aqoḇ, has sent me to you. This is <dn>My Name</dn> forever, and this is <dn>My</dn> remembrance to all generations.’</dq> [16] <dq>Go, and you shall gather <dn>את</dn> the elders of Yisra’el together, and say to them, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of your fathers, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, of Yitsḥaq, and of Ya’aqoḇ, appeared to me, saying, “<dn>I</dn> have indeed visited <dn>את</dn> you and seen <dn>את</dn> what is done to you in Mitsrayim;</dq> [17] <dq>and <dn>I</dn> say: <dn>I</dn> am bringing you up out of the affliction of Mitsrayim to the land of the Kena’anite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hiwwite and the Yeḇusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.” ’</dq> [18] And they shall listen to your voice. And you shall come, you and the elders of Yisra’el, to the sovereign of Mitsrayim, and you shall say to him, ‘YeHoVaH Elohim of the Heḇrews has met with us. And now, please, let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness to offer to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ [19] But <dn>I</dn> know that the sovereign of Mitsrayim is not going to let you go, not even by a <dn>strong hand</dn>. [20] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall stretch out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My hand</dn> and strike <dn>את</dn> Mitsrayim with all <dn>My</dn> wonders which <dn>I</dn> shall do in its midst, and after that he shall let <dn>את</dn> you go.</dq> [21] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give this people <dn>את</dn> favour in the eyes of the Mitsrites. And it shall be, that when you go, you shall not go empty-handed.</dq> [22] <dq>But every woman shall ask of her neighbour, and of her who sojourns in her house, items of silver, and items of gold, and garments. And you shall put them on your sons and on your daughters, and shall plunder <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrites.”</dq>

readings.title: Signs for Moses and the Calling of Aaron
readings.subtitle: Three Signs and a Partner
readings.text: [Exodus 4:1] And Mosheh answered and said, “And if they do not believe me, nor listen to my voice, and say, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not appeared to you’?” [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“What is that in your hand?”</dq> And he said, “A rod.” [3] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Throw it on the ground.”</dq> So he threw it on the ground, and it became a serpent. And Mosheh fled from it. [4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Reach out your hand and take it by the tail”</dq> – so he reached out his hand and caught it, and it became a rod in his hand – [5] <dq>“so that they believe that <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of their fathers, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yitsḥaq, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya’aqoḇ, has appeared to you.”</dq> [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him again, <dq>“Now put your hand into your bosom.”</dq> And he put his hand into his bosom, and when he took it out, see, his hand was leprous, like snow. [7] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Put your hand back into your bosom.”</dq> So he put his hand back into his bosom, and when he took it out from his bosom, see, it was restored like his other flesh. [8] <dq>“And it shall be, if they do not believe you, nor listen to the voice of the first sign, they shall believe the voice of the latter sign.</dq> [9] <dq>And it shall be, if they do not believe even these two signs, nor listen to your voice, that you shall take water from the river and pour it on the dry land. And the water which you take from the river shall become blood on the dry land.”</dq> [10] And Mosheh said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, I am not a man of words, neither yesterday nor since <dn>You</dn> have spoken to <dn>Your</dn> servant, for I am slow of mouth and slow of tongue.” [11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Who has made man’s mouth? Or who makes the dumb, or the deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? Is it not <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?</dq> [12] <dq>And now, go, and <dn>I</dn> am with your mouth and shall teach you <dn>את</dn> what you are to say.”</dq> [13] And he said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please send by the hand of him whom <dn>You</dn> would send.” [14] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Mosheh, and <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Is not Aharon the Lĕwite your brother? <dn>I</dn> know that he speaks well. And see, he is also coming out to meet you. And when he sees you, he shall be glad in <dn>his heart</dn>.</dq> [15] <dq>And you shall speak to him and put <dn>את</dn> the words in his mouth. And <dn>I</dn> am with your mouth and with his mouth, and shall teach <dn>את</dn> you <dn>את</dn> what you are to do.</dq> [16] <dq>And he shall speak for you to the people. And it shall be that he shall be a mouth for you, and you shall be an elohim for him.</dq> [17] <dq>And you shall take <dn>את</dn> this rod in your hand, with which you shall do <dn>את</dn> the signs.”</dq>
